messages:
Anna (ML): Heads up — new 8-bit quantized reranker (v2-q8) shows ~3.2% NDCG drop in prod compared to baseline. Local eval on eval-harness didn't show regression. Anyone seen batching/seed repro issues?
Rui: Did you run with same random seed and batch ordering? Prod uses dynamic batching and request sharding.
Anna (ML): I locked seed=42 in our eval harness. Prod logs show varying seeds (null). See config snippet:
```yaml
seed: null
eval_batch: 16
dynamic_batching: true
kv_cache_enabled: true
max_seq: 512
```
Maya: dynamic batching can change input order and therefore per-batch normalization stats in some scorers. Reranker uses layernorm — but that's deterministic; maybe it's due to mixed precision accumulation? :thinking:
Sam: Also check tokenization/truncation differences — prod truncates at 512 with right-side truncation, local left. That can flip doc context.
Anna (ML): ack — tokenizer config differed (truncation_side). Fixing to right-side gave 1.1% NDCG back locally.
Rui: Another thing — prod uses asynchronous KV cache reuse across requests when serving pairwise reranks to save compute. If the cache warm-up differs it may affect early tokens and beam order.
Anna (ML): here's minimal repro I ran in a loop that *does* flip scores depending on batch composition:
```
# pseudo
for reqs in [random.shuffle(qs, seed=42), ordered_qs]:
  scores = rerank_batch(reqs, batch_size=32, quant=True)
  print(mean_ndcg(scores))
```
Maya: can you attach the specific sample IDs that flip? I can run on dedicated infra without dynamic batching.
Anna (ML): attached a small CSV id list (uploaded to s3://redwood-evals/tmp/flip_ids.csv). Quick checks show ~120 queries flip at top-1.
deploy-bot: prod-deploy v2-q8 completed at 2025-11-19T14:23:10Z :rocket:
Sam: For immediate mitigation, enable deterministic batching in prod for the next canary and re-run smoke NDCG checks.
Anna (ML): will try deterministic canary + align tokenizer/truncation + set seed to 42. I'll post results.
Maya: upvote for adding a unit-test in eval-harness that compares static vs dynamic batching behavior so we don't regress.
Rui: +1. Also add a perf note: deterministic batching may increase latency tail.
Anna (ML): thanks all — will follow up with numbers in ~30m. :thumbsup:
